findings.description: `Expect` is forwarded but never honoured, and `status<200` makes a `100 Continue` abort the exchange into a flat `502`. The client's request body — a whole `GET /api%2fexec%20?cmd=uname%20-a` line, sent with `Content-Length: 0` on the outer POST — is then re-parsed as the next request, decoded and executed upstream. One client request returns two heads (`502` then `200` with `SEQ:2 EXEC:uid=1000`), 6/6 deterministic, and the effect survives a non-exec isolation POST so the `uid` output cannot come from request 1. Precondition: a proxy location plus an upstream that actually emits `100 Continue`.
findings.title: The upstream's interim `100` is rejected as a parse failure, and the leftover request body is re-parsed as a second request that executes

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
